INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.

2. When practising Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.

3. When practising Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency.

4. When practising Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas.

5. When practising Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 3.2.1 Reading for comprehension.

6. When practising Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.3.1 Punctuation.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Information.

8. In INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   C. Only memorise without using the language
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

9. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Attentive Listening.

   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
